title: Production class-group service and reactor
objective: Promote the qualified public cubic completion and resident query protocol into packages/class-groups, produce a native resident service and bounded Wasm reactor from the same source, and add exact protocol/lifecycle tests

oracles: Existing public-cubic-e2e and Wasm resident-session qualification suites

handoff.summary: Promoted the qualified exact public-cubic completion and arbitrary-ideal witness route into the production class-groups package. Added one bounded generation-aware protocol shared by a resident native JSON-lines service and Wasm reactor, including a compact summary boundary with exact integral canonical class-generator ideals that avoids detaching the bulk relation graph. The service provides deterministic authority receipts, typed errors, fixed-width wire resource counters, one authenticated GMP/MPFR allocator domain, and exact lifecycle tests. The initial qualified Wasm reactor was 6,302,427 bytes, with one internal memory having a 16 MiB initial size and 256 MiB maximum, and SHA-256 bc5bdafe872dc21bcd15e5185073a14fbefec599735dca36aa01e4f5491047e8; packaging must regenerate and authenticate the final follow-up source.
risks: The generated dist artifact is intentionally ignored and must be rebuilt and authenticated by the packaging lane rather than committed.
The new Rust boundary files must be registered in architecture/native-code.json by the integration lane because that shared inventory is outside this task's claims.

macOS qualification must occur only after the product Cargo changes and the safety lane's exact FLINT/GMP/MPFR archive identity enforcement are integrated; the prior branch configuration could build a second private GMP.
next_steps: Integrate this commit with the provenance/safety bridge changes, then register the new service and reactor in the shared native-code inventory.
Package and authenticate class-group-service and class-group-core.wasm, wiring the host adapter to add artifactSha256 at its trusted boundary.
Run the frozen lifecycle and row-6 product tests through Node and browser workers on Linux and macOS, then complete native Windows capability/fallback qualification.
